intro: Here legend meets the earth. You are at Troy, a mound in Çanakkale province, whose story reaches back to 3000 BC. Beneath your feet lie nine cities, one on top of another — the legendary mound behind Homer's Iliad.
history: People lived here for 5,000 years. In the 1870s Heinrich Schliemann excavated the mound. He proved the legend was real — but in doing so, he damaged its layers.
structure-1: Look now at the city walls, the citadel walls of Troy in the Late Bronze Age. The lower wall is dressed limestone with a sloping, battered face that steps back a little every few metres, and mud brick once stood on top of it. The East Gate is not an opening through the wall but a passage climbing between two of its ends; beyond it a tower stands forward of the wall, and on the terraces inside stood large free-standing houses.
structure-5: And here stands the Trojan horse replica, a copy of the famous wooden horse from Homer's Iliad. Look up at it and imagine the story that made it immortal.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the ramped gateway, the Odeon and the Temple of Athena.
facts: Did you know? Nine cities stand stacked in this mound, and Homer's Troy is most likely level VI/VII. Digging in 1871, Schliemann drove straight past the layer he was looking for and found his 'Treasure of Priam' in one a thousand years too old. No trace of the wooden horse has ever been found. Hittite tablets, however, record treaties with a city called Wilusa, in the right place to be Troy. And the battered stone wall of the citadel is taken for the one that Patroclus climbs three times in the Iliad — and is thrown back from three times.
outro: This brings our tour of Troy to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These walls have outlasted heroes and legends; let them stand for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
